answer.explanation: The service validates the request and builds Locations. It then gathers open pools and builds Candidate objects through this.candidates(...), which carry addedSeconds and withoutSeconds for each pool. It falls back to estimates when the drive-time quota is exhausted, and a matching policy picks one candidate. The chosen Pool then gets take(...) and is saved. The route-time calculation per pool may be business logic over aggregate state done in the service. But the body of candidates() isn't shown, so I can't see whether it reads the pool's internal state or delegates to the pool. The service also doesn't pass the computed result into the aggregate, because take receives only the rider and locations. The code shown doesn't settle it.
